[AMD][Gluon] Add descriptor buffer ops for gfx1250 (#12512)

Expose the descriptor-based buffer ops on gfx1250 as
`ttgl.amd.gfx1250.buffer` (`cdna5.buffer`): `make_buffer_descriptor`,
`load` and `store`, with `soffset`, `scope` and a gfx1250 `CachePolicy`.
gfx1250 has no buffer loads to LDS, so there is no `load_to_shared`.

- `#amdg.cache_policy_gfx1250<temporal = ...>` sets the TH field:
  regular, nontemporal, high_temporal or, for loads only, last_use. TH 3
  means write-back on stores and a cache bypass at system scope, so the
  verifier rejects last_use on stores and with the sys scope.
- `scope` sets the SCOPE field as LLVM's gfx125x memory model does: cta
  = SCOPE_CU (the default, as a workgroup runs on one WGP), gpu =
  SCOPE_DEV and sys = SCOPE_SYS.

Bounds, as measured on gfx1250: soffset is counted, an access that ends
within num_records is in bounds as a whole, and masking with a
0xFFFFFFFF offset holds for any 32-bit num_records. Unlike gfx950, an
access that crosses num_records keeps only its 4-byte pieces that end at
least 4 bytes before it, so vectorized accesses near the bound can drop
elements that fit. num_records stays 32-bit for now although the gfx1250
V# holds 45 bits.

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+"""Cache policy hints for CDNA5 memory accesses."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from triton.language.core import constexpr_type
+from ..._core import _unwrap_if_constexpr
+
+__all__ = ["CachePolicy"]
+
+_TEMPORAL_HINTS = ("regular", "none", "high", "last_use")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class CachePolicy:
+    """
+    Cache hints for CDNA5 memory accesses, taken by the ``buffer`` ops.
+
+    The hints are performance-only and never affect coherence. The coherence
+    scope of an access comes from the op's ``scope=`` argument instead.
+
+    Args:
+        temporal (str): How long the data is expected to stay in the caches (TH): ``"regular"``,
+            ``"none"`` (not expected to be reused), ``"high"`` (expected to be reused) or, for loads
+            only, ``"last_use"`` (the last read of the data, which the caches can drop).
+            ``"last_use"`` can't be combined with the ``"sys"`` scope.
+    """
+
+    temporal: str = "regular"
+
+    def __post_init__(self):
+        temporal = _unwrap_if_constexpr(self.temporal)
+        if temporal not in _TEMPORAL_HINTS:
+            raise ValueError(f"temporal must be one of {_TEMPORAL_HINTS}, got {temporal!r}")
+        object.__setattr__(self, "temporal", temporal)
+
+    @property
+    def type(self):
+        return constexpr_type(self)
+
+    def mangle(self) -> str:
+        return f"AMDCP_gfx12_{self.temporal}_AMDCP"
+
+    def _to_ir(self, builder):
+        return builder.get_amd_cache_policy_gfx12(self.temporal)

@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+"""
+Descriptor-based buffer memory ops for CDNA5.
+
+These access global memory through an explicit buffer resource descriptor (:func:`make_buffer_descriptor`)
+instead of a base pointer, with explicit bounds, a scalar offset and per-access coherence scope. The
+pointer-based ``buffer_load`` / ``buffer_store`` in the parent module are unchanged but will be deprecated and
+migrated to these ops soon.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from ..._core import builtin
+from .. import _buffer
+from .._buffer import buffer_descriptor, buffer_descriptor_type
+from ..cdna3.buffer import _format_doc
+from ._cache_policy import CachePolicy as _CachePolicy
+
+__all__ = ["buffer_descriptor", "buffer_descriptor_type", "make_buffer_descriptor", "load", "store"]
+
+
+@builtin
+def make_buffer_descriptor(base, num_records, _semantic=None) -> buffer_descriptor:
+    """
+    Make a buffer resource descriptor from the hardware fields the program controls.
+
+    Accesses through the descriptor address ``base + soffset + offsets[i]``. The hardware checks every
+    access against ``num_records``, counting ``soffset``: in bytes from ``base``, an access is in bounds
+    only if ``soffset + offset + size <= num_records``. Out-of-bounds loads return zero and out-of-bounds
+    stores are dropped, so ``num_records=0`` disables every access.
+
+    The check applies per hardware access, not per element. An access that ends within ``num_records`` is
+    in bounds as a whole. One that crosses it is checked in 4-byte pieces, and a piece is in bounds only if
+    it ends at least 4 bytes before ``num_records``, so elements near the bound can be out of bounds even
+    though they fit. How many elements an access holds is up to the compiler: it vectorizes based on the
+    alignment of ``base`` and ``offsets`` and on the mask, but not on ``num_records``. So near the bound,
+    the result can depend on vectorization. For example, loading ``offsets = [0, 1, 2, ...]`` (a store
+    drops the same elements):
+
+    - int32 elements and ``num_records = 20``: with one element per access, elements 0 to 4 are loaded.
+      With four per access (16 bytes), the access holding elements 4 to 7 crosses the bound, and element
+      4 reads zero too: its piece ends at byte 20, not 4 bytes before the bound.
+    - int8 elements and ``num_records = 10``: with one element per access, elements 0 to 9 are loaded.
+      With sixteen per access, the access holding elements 0 to 15 crosses the bound, and only its first
+      piece (elements 0 to 3) is in bounds.
+
+    To bound each element exactly, keep accesses from crossing ``num_records``: make it and ``soffset``
+    (in bytes) multiples of 16 bytes, the widest access, or also mask the elements past the bound, e.g.
+    ``mask=offsets < n`` with ``num_records = n * 4`` for int32 and no ``soffset``. The compiler only
+    vectorizes an access as far as its mask allows, so no access the mask keeps crosses the bound.
+
+    The descriptor is as aligned as ``base``: use :func:`~triton.experimental.gluon.language.multiple_of`
+    on ``base`` to let accesses through it vectorize when the compiler can't prove the alignment.
+
+    Args:
+        base (pointer to scalar): Global memory base pointer. Its pointee type is the element type of
+            the descriptor; offsets count these elements.
+        num_records (int32 or uint32 scalar): Bytes accessible from ``base``, read as an unsigned 32-bit
+            value: up to 2**32 - 1.
+
+    Returns:
+        buffer_descriptor: the descriptor.
+    """
+    return _buffer.make_buffer_descriptor(base, num_records, _semantic)
+
+
+@builtin
+@_format_doc
+def load(desc, offsets, mask=None, other=None, *, soffset=None, scope=None, cache_policy=None, _semantic=None):
+    """
+    Load from global memory through a buffer descriptor into registers.
+
+    Element ``i`` is read from ``base + soffset + offsets[i]``. Out-of-bounds elements read zero, and
+    masked-off elements read ``other``, or zero without it. See :func:`make_buffer_descriptor` for the
+    bounds.
+
+    Args:
+        desc (buffer_descriptor): Descriptor of the global memory to load from.
+        offsets (tensor): Offsets of the elements to load, in elements.
+        mask (tensor, optional): Mask tensor for predicated loads. Defaults to None.
+        other (tensor or scalar, optional): Values for masked-off elements. Defaults to None.
+        scope (str, optional): ``"cta"``, ``"gpu"`` or ``"sys"``. The load reads data visible at that
+            scope. It is not atomic and orders no other memory operation; pair it with an acquire to
+            consume a payload. To poll a flag, use :func:`~triton.experimental.gluon.language.atomic_load`
+            instead, which the compiler never hoists. Defaults to None (coherent within the
+            workgroup).
+        {soffset_arg}
+        cache_policy (:class:`~triton.experimental.gluon.language.amd.cdna5.CachePolicy`, optional): Cache
+            hints. Defaults to None.
+
+    Returns:
+        tensor: The loaded values, with the shape and layout of ``offsets``.
+    """
+    return _buffer.load(desc, offsets, mask, other, soffset, scope, cache_policy, _CachePolicy, _semantic)
+
+
+@builtin
+@_format_doc
+def store(value, desc, offsets, mask=None, *, soffset=None, scope=None, cache_policy=None, _semantic=None):
+    """
+    Store a tensor to global memory through a buffer descriptor.
+
+    Element ``i`` is written to ``base + soffset + offsets[i]``. Out-of-bounds and masked-off elements
+    are dropped. See :func:`make_buffer_descriptor` for the bounds.
+
+    Args:
+        value (tensor): The values to store.
+        desc (buffer_descriptor): Descriptor of the global memory to store to.
+        offsets (tensor): Offsets of the elements to store, in elements.
+        mask (tensor, optional): Mask tensor for predicated stores. Defaults to None.
+        scope (str, optional): ``"cta"``, ``"gpu"`` or ``"sys"``. The store makes its data available at
+            that scope. It is not atomic and orders no other memory operation; follow it with a release
+            to publish. Defaults to None.
+        {soffset_arg}
+        cache_policy (:class:`~triton.experimental.gluon.language.amd.cdna5.CachePolicy`, optional): Cache
+            hints. Defaults to None.
+    """
+    _buffer.store(value, desc, offsets, mask, soffset, scope, cache_policy, _CachePolicy, _semantic)

+// RUN: triton-opt %s -split-input-file --allocate-shared-memory --convert-triton-amdgpu-to-llvm=gfx-arch=gfx1250 | FileCheck %s
+
+// A buffer descriptor packs its base and num_records into the resource;
+// soffset feeds the instruction's scalar offset, scaled from elements to bytes.
+
+#blocked = #ttg.blocked<{sizePerThread = [1], threadsPerWarp = [32], warpsPerCTA = [1], order = [0]}>
+module attributes {"ttg.num-ctas" = 1 : i32, "ttg.num-warps" = 1 : i32, "ttg.threads-per-warp" = 32 : i32} {
+  // CHECK-LABEL: buffer_desc_soffset
+  tt.func @buffer_desc_soffset(%arg0: !tt.ptr<f32>, %offsets: tensor<32xi32, #blocked>, %s: i32, %n: i32) {
+    // CHECK: %[[STRIDE:.*]] = llvm.mlir.constant(0 : i16) : i16
+    // CHECK: %[[NUM:.*]] = llvm.zext %{{.*}} : i32 to i64
+    // CHECK: %[[RSRC:.*]] = rocdl.make.buffer.rsrc %{{.*}}, %[[STRIDE]], %[[NUM]], %{{.*}}
+    %desc = amdg.make_buffer_desc %arg0, %n : !tt.ptr<f32> -> !amdg.buffer_desc<f32>
+    // CHECK: %[[C4:.*]] = llvm.mlir.constant(4 : i32) : i32
+    // CHECK: %[[SOFF:.*]] = llvm.mul %[[C4]], %{{.*}} : i32
+    // CHECK: rocdl.raw.ptr.buffer.load %[[RSRC]], %{{.*}}, %[[SOFF]], 0 : f32
+    %0 = amdg.buffer_load %desc[%offsets] soffset = %s : i32 : !amdg.buffer_desc<f32> -> tensor<32xf32, #blocked>
+    // CHECK: rocdl.raw.ptr.buffer.store %{{.*}}, %[[RSRC]], %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, 0 : f32
+    amdg.buffer_store %0, %desc[%offsets] soffset = %s : i32 : !amdg.buffer_desc<f32> -> tensor<32xf32, #blocked>
+    tt.return
+  }
+}
+
+// -----
+
+// scope selects SCOPE and the gfx12 policy selects TH, independently.
+
+#blocked = #ttg.blocked<{sizePerThread = [1], threadsPerWarp = [32], warpsPerCTA = [1], order = [0]}>
+module attributes {"ttg.num-ctas" = 1 : i32, "ttg.num-warps" = 1 : i32, "ttg.threads-per-warp" = 32 : i32} {
+  // CHECK-LABEL: buffer_scope_policy
+  tt.func @buffer_scope_policy(%arg0: !tt.ptr<f32>, %offsets: tensor<32xi32, #blocked>) {
+    // CHECK: rocdl.raw.ptr.buffer.load %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, 1 : f32
+    %0 = amdg.buffer_load %arg0[%offsets] {cachePolicy = #amdg.cache_policy_gfx12<temporal = none>} : !tt.ptr<f32> -> tensor<32xf32, #blocked>
+    // CHECK: rocdl.raw.ptr.buffer.load %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, 0 : f32
+    %1 = amdg.buffer_load %arg0[%offsets] {scope = 2 : i32} : !tt.ptr<f32> -> tensor<32xf32, #blocked>
+    // CHECK: rocdl.raw.ptr.buffer.load %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, 19 : f32
+    %2 = amdg.buffer_load %arg0[%offsets] {scope = 1 : i32, cachePolicy = #amdg.cache_policy_gfx12<temporal = last_use>} : !tt.ptr<f32> -> tensor<32xf32, #blocked>
+    // CHECK: rocdl.raw.ptr.buffer.store %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, 26 : f32
+    amdg.buffer_store %0, %arg0[%offsets] {scope = 3 : i32, cachePolicy = #amdg.cache_policy_gfx12<temporal = high>} : !tt.ptr<f32> -> tensor<32xf32, #blocked>
+    tt.return
+  }
+}

     torch.testing.assert_close(c_device.cpu(), torch.bmm(a.float(), b.float()), rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_hip_cdna5(), reason="Requires CDNA5")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("vec", [1, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("soffset, num_elements", [(0, 40), (10, 40), (30, 60), (10, 5), (5, 0), (0, 41)])
+def test_buffer_descriptor_soffset_bounds_cdna5(vec, soffset, num_elements):
+
+    @gluon.jit
+    def kernel(src, dst, soffset, num_elements, VEC: ttgl.constexpr):
+        layout: ttgl.constexpr = ttgl.BlockedLayout([VEC], [32], [1], [0])
+        offsets = ttgl.arange(0, 32 * VEC, layout=layout)
+        # Without a stride, num_records counts bytes and bounds soffset + offsets.
+        src_desc = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.make_buffer_descriptor(src, num_elements * 4)
+        x = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.load(src_desc, offsets, soffset=soffset)
+        ttgl.store(dst + offsets, x)
+        dst_desc = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.make_buffer_descriptor(dst + 32 * VEC, num_elements * 4)
+        ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.store(x + 1, dst_desc, offsets, soffset=soffset)
+
+    n = 32 * vec
+    src = torch.arange(1000, 1000 + 2 * n, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    dst = torch.full((3 * n, ), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    compiled = kernel[(1, )](src, dst, soffset, num_elements, vec, num_warps=1)
+
+    index = torch.arange(n, device="cuda")
+    num_records = num_elements * 4
+    end = (soffset + index + 1) * 4
+    access_end = (soffset + (index // vec + 1) * vec) * 4
+    # An access partly out of bounds keeps only its 4-byte pieces that end at
+    # least 4 bytes before num_records.
+    in_bounds = (access_end <= num_records) | (end + 4 <= num_records)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(dst[:n], torch.where(in_bounds, src[soffset + index], 0).int(), atol=0, rtol=0)
+    stored = torch.full((2 * n, ), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    loaded = dst[:n]
+    stored[(soffset + index)[in_bounds]] = loaded[in_bounds] + 1
+    torch.testing.assert_close(dst[n:], stored, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    # soffset stays in a scalar register.
+    load = "buffer_load_b32" if vec == 1 else "buffer_load_b128"
+    assert re.search(rf"{load} v(\d+|\[\d+:\d+\]), v\d+, s\[\d+:\d+\], s\d+ offen", compiled.asm["amdgcn"])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_hip_cdna5(), reason="Requires CDNA5")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.int8, torch.int32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lane_bytes", ["element", 16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_records", [2**31, 2**32 - 4, 2**32 - 1])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("soffset", [0, 5])
+def test_buffer_descriptor_full_range_mask_cdna5(dtype, lane_bytes, num_records, soffset):
+    elem_bytes = dtype.itemsize
+    vec = 1 if lane_bytes == "element" else 16 // elem_bytes
+    gl_dtype = getattr(ttgl, str(dtype).removeprefix("torch."))
+
+    @gluon.jit
+    def kernel(src, dst, out, num_records, soffset, VEC: ttgl.constexpr, DTYPE: ttgl.constexpr):
+        layout: ttgl.constexpr = ttgl.BlockedLayout([VEC], [32], [1], [0])
+        offsets = ttgl.arange(0, 32 * VEC, layout=layout)
+        # Every other lane is masked off as a whole, keeping its access vectorized.
+        mask = (offsets // VEC) % 2 == 0
+        # With a bound at or above 2**31, masked-off lanes must still be dropped.
+        bound = num_records.to(ttgl.uint32)
+        src_desc = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.make_buffer_descriptor(src, bound)
+        x = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.load(src_desc, offsets, mask=mask, other=-5, soffset=soffset)
+        ttgl.store(out + offsets, x)
+        dst_desc = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.make_buffer_descriptor(dst, bound)
+        ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.store(offsets.to(DTYPE) + 1, dst_desc, offsets, mask=mask, soffset=soffset)
+
+    n = 32 * vec
+    src = (torch.arange(soffset + n, device="cuda") % 100 + 1).to(dtype)
+    dst = torch.full((soffset + n, ), -1, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+    out = torch.empty(n, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+    compiled = kernel[(1, )](src, dst, out, num_records, soffset, vec, gl_dtype, num_warps=1)
+
+    index = torch.arange(n, device="cuda")
+    active = (index // vec) % 2 == 0
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, torch.where(active, src[soffset:], -5).to(dtype), atol=0, rtol=0)
+    expected_dst = torch.full((soffset + n, ), -1, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+    expected_dst[soffset:] = torch.where(active, index + 1, -1).to(dtype)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(dst, expected_dst, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    if lane_bytes == 16:
+        amdgcn = compiled.asm["amdgcn"]
+        assert "buffer_load_b128" in amdgcn and "buffer_store_b128" in amdgcn
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_hip_cdna5(), reason="Requires CDNA5")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scope, scope_bits", [(None, ""), ("cta", ""), ("gpu", " scope:SCOPE_DEV"),
+                                               ("sys", " scope:SCOPE_SYS")])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("temporal", [None, "none", "high"])
+def test_buffer_load_store_scope_cache_policy_cdna5(scope, scope_bits, temporal):
+
+    @gluon.jit
+    def kernel(src, dst, scope: ttgl.constexpr, temporal: ttgl.constexpr):
+        layout: ttgl.constexpr = ttgl.BlockedLayout([1], [32], [1], [0])
+        offsets = ttgl.arange(0, 32, layout=layout)
+        if temporal is None:
+            policy: ttgl.constexpr = None
+        else:
+            policy: ttgl.constexpr = ttgl.amd.cdna5.CachePolicy(temporal=temporal)
+        src_desc = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.make_buffer_descriptor(src, 32 * 4)
+        dst_desc = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.make_buffer_descriptor(dst, 32 * 4)
+        x = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.load(src_desc, offsets, scope=scope, cache_policy=policy)
+        ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.store(x, dst_desc, offsets, scope=scope, cache_policy=policy)
+
+    src = torch.arange(32, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    dst = torch.empty_like(src)
+    compiled = kernel[(1, )](src, dst, scope, temporal, num_warps=1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(dst, src, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+    def bits(instruction):
+        match = re.search(rf"^\s*{instruction} v\d+, v\d+, s\[\d+:\d+\], null offen(.*)$", compiled.asm["amdgcn"],
+                          re.MULTILINE)
+        assert match, instruction
+        return set(match.group(1).split())
+
+    th = {None: set(), "none": {"th:TH_{}_NT"}, "high": {"th:TH_{}_HT"}}[temporal]
+    assert bits("buffer_load_b32") == set(scope_bits.split()) | {t.format("LOAD") for t in th}
+    assert bits("buffer_store_b32") == set(scope_bits.split()) | {t.format("STORE") for t in th}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_hip_cdna5(), reason="Requires CDNA5")
+def test_buffer_load_last_use_cdna5():
+
+    @gluon.jit
+    def kernel(src, dst):
+        layout: ttgl.constexpr = ttgl.BlockedLayout([1], [32], [1], [0])
+        offsets = ttgl.arange(0, 32, layout=layout)
+        policy: ttgl.constexpr = ttgl.amd.cdna5.CachePolicy(temporal="last_use")
+        src_desc = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.make_buffer_descriptor(src, 32 * 4)
+        x = ttgl.amd.cdna5.buffer.load(src_desc, offsets, scope="gpu", cache_policy=policy)
+        ttgl.store(dst + offsets, x)
+
+    src = torch.arange(32, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    dst = torch.empty_like(src)
+    compiled = kernel[(1, )](src, dst, num_warps=1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(dst, src, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    assert re.search(r"buffer_load_b32 .* th:TH_LOAD_LU scope:SCOPE_DEV$", compiled.asm["amdgcn"], re.MULTILINE)

[BC-Breaking][Libdevice] Remove fma and fma_rn, redundant with tl.fma (#12558)

## Summary

`tl.fma` lowers to MLIR `math.fma` (round-to-nearest-even), so the
libdevice
`fma` (`__nv_fmaf`/`__nv_fma`, `__ocml_fma_f32`/`f64`) and `fma_rn`
(`__nv_fmaf_rn`/`__nv_fma_rn`) wrappers duplicate a core language
builtin.
The non-default rounding variants `fma_rz`/`fma_rd`/`fma_ru` have no
core
equivalent yet and are kept.

## Changes

adding a rounding mode to `tl.fma` as a followup.

[TRITONGPU] Remove unnecessary layout conversions in CGA assignment (#12552)

We can slice through a DAG instead of a tree. In the following cases no
layout conversion is required

before this PR we will have two convert layouts.
```
%b = tt.descriptor_load ... -> tensor<32x128xf16, #dot_b_old>
%b0 = ttg.convert_layout %b ... -> tensor<32x128xf16, #dot_b_new>
%d0 = tt.dot ..., %b0, ...
%b1 = ttg.convert_layout %b ... -> tensor<32x128xf16, #dot_b_new>
%d1 = tt.dot ..., %b1, ...
```
after this PR convert layouts are removed
```
%b = tt.descriptor_load ... -> tensor<32x128xf16, #dot_b_new>
%d0 = tt.dot ..., %b, ...
%d1 = tt.dot ..., %b, ...
```

[AMD] Use hardware tanh for fast_tanhf on CDNA5, keep tanh exact (#12560)

## Summary

CDNA5 (gfx1250) adds a native `V_TANH` instruction (F32/F16/BF16) that
was not present in CDNA4. The hardware tanh is a cubic approximation
(ISA: identity below 2^-10, saturate at >= 8, `TanhCubicApproximation`
in between), so it belongs behind the approximate `fast_` API, not the
precise one. This PR:

- **`libdevice.fast_tanhf`** (`__triton_hip_fast_tanhf`): on CDNA5,
lower to `llvm.amdgcn.tanh.f32` (single transcendental op instead of the
~8-op stable exp expansion with two transcendental-pipe ops). All other
targets keep the current formula.
- **`libdevice.tanh`** (`__ocml_tanh_f32`): remove the CDNA5 intercept
that lowered precise tanh to the approximate hardware instruction, so
`tanh` uses the exact OCML implementation on every arch. This matches
NVIDIA semantics: precise `__nv_tanhf` is exact software,
`__nv_fast_tanhf` -> `tanh.approx.f32` is the approximate hardware path.

## Test Plan

`lit -v test/Conversion/amd/builtin_func_to_llvm.mlir`

- gfx1250 (ftz on/off): `fast_tanhf` emits `llvm.amdgcn.tanh.f32` with
no exp2 formula; `tanh` stays an `__ocml_tanh_f32` call
- gfx942/gfx950: `fast_tanhf` keeps the exp2-formula fallback

Verified by building `triton-opt` and running the lit test (all RUN
lines pass).

## TODO before ready

Numeric validation of the hardware cubic vs the old `fast_tanhf` formula
on real gfx1250 (max ULP, >= 8 saturation, < 2^-10 identity region,
Inf/NaN). Note the precise-`tanh` change is a numerics change for
existing CDNA5 users (approx hardware -> exact OCML); it restores
cross-arch/cross-vendor consistency for the precise API.

[FRONTEND] Normalize negative dim in sort/topk (#12559)

`tl.sort`, `tl.topk` and `tl.bitonic_merge` reject `dim=-1`:

```
tl.sort(x, dim=-1)  # CompileTimeAssertionFailure: only minor dimension is currently supported
```

even though -1 is the minor dimension. Normalize `dim` with
`core._wrap_axis` before the check. It's wrapped with
`constexpr_function` in standard.py so it can be called from `@jit`
code, like `get_int_dtype`. Any other dim is still rejected with the
same message, and an out-of-range dim now gets `_wrap_axis`'s "invalid
axis" error.

`test_sort_negative_dim` calls `tl.sort`, `tl.topk` and
`tl.bitonic_merge` with `dim=-1` and compares against torch. It fails
without this change. I ran it with `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` and checked the
compiled path through the frontend, but haven't run it on a GPU.
